name: 01_coast_west
what: the W coast: the plateau, the shingle beach falling to the shore ice, the first sea cliffs

name: 02_wreck_beach
what: the wreck heeled in the shore ice at the foot of the shingle beach

name: 03_cliffs_south
what: the S sea cliffs (6-8 m): rock-kit columns, talus, a stack in the shore-fast ice

name: 04_cove_close
what: CLOSE: the sea-cut cove -- the cave in its back wall, the small iced landing, the stair cut inland between rock columns

name: 05_cave_mouth
what: the cave mouth: a dark wave-worn arch, 7 m clear; the sea and floes reach into it

name: 06_mere
what: the mere (~440 m2): plated ice, thin cracks over the whole of it, reed islands

name: 07_pack_ice
what: the sea: broken pack -- plates of every size, rims, ridges, brash, dark leads (~2/3 ice)

name: 08_start
what: the start in the stone circle (4 standing, 2 fallen low blocks)

name: 09_stair_close
what: CLOSE: the stair -- every tread its own stone (snow on top, bare stone at the front), 5 m clear, climbing inland

name: 10_cove_wide
what: WIDE: the cove in the cliff line -- vertical rock columns either side, the cave, the landing, the stair cleft

name: 11_mere_sea
what: the mere turning into the sea through one graded ice field and reed islands (R-C9-221)

name: 12_river_mere
what: the river entering at the top-left, down beside the coast into the mere (R-C9-222/223)

name: 13_hall_yard
what: the burnt hall's ash yard: an irregular trampled patch, no straight edges
